title: Etale equivalence relations have algebraic-space quotients
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $V$ a scheme over $S$. Let $(s,t):R\to V\times_SV$ [def-pc-fibre-product] be a monomorphism of schemes such that for every $S$-scheme $T$ the image of $R(T)$ in $V(T)\times V(T)$ is an equivalence relation, and assume $s$ and $t$ are etale [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Let $F$ be the sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification], for the big fppf site $(\mathit{Sch}/S)_{fppf}$ [def-pc-fppf-site], of the presheaf $T\mapsto V(T)/R(T)$. Then $F$ is an algebraic space [def-trf-algebraic-space], $q:h_V\to F$ is etale and surjective, and the map $h_R\to h_V\times_Fh_V$ induced by $(s,t)$ is an isomorphism. In particular, every section of $F$ over a scheme lifts to $V$ on an etale covering. For any fppf sheaf $G$, composition with $q$ is a bijection between maps $F\to G$ and maps $h_V\to G$ whose composites with $s,t$ agree.

source.place: Tag 02WW (theorem-presentation); Tag 02WV (lemma-when-it-works-it-works), with the presentation kernel-pair identity and the defining sheaf quotient universal property.

proof.text: First let $g:U'\to U$ be a surjective etale morphism. By [lem-trf-etale-relation-restriction-quotient], the restricted relation is etale and the quotient map is an isomorphism when $g$ is surjective. Thus a surjective etale refinement of the atlas may be used without changing the quotient.

source.place: Tag 02WW, first reduction, using Tags 02VH and 02WT.

proof.text: Choose an affine open covering $U=\bigcup_iU_i$ and let $U'=\coprod_iU_i\to U$ be the resulting surjective etale map. The scheme coproduct lemma [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family] makes $U'$ a scheme with the $U_i$ as pairwise disjoint open-and-closed summands. The restriction lemma, applied first to $U'\to U$ and then to each (generally non-surjective) etale summand inclusion $U_i\to U'$, shows that every restricted relation $R_i$ is etale; it does not identify an individual quotient $F_i=U_i/R_i$ with $F$.

source.place: Tag 02WW, first and second paragraphs: replace by an affine coproduct and restrict the relation.

proof.text: For each affine $U_i$, apply [lem-trf-etale-affine-quotient-representable]. It gives representability of every base change of $h_{U_i}\to F_i$ and representability of the diagonal of $F_i$. The kernel-pair lemma [lem-trf-etale-relation-kernel-pair] identifies $h_{R_i}$ with $h_{U_i}\times_{F_i}h_{U_i}$. For an fppf presentation $T_j\to T$ of a section of $F_i$, this identification gives $T_j\times_{F_i}h_{U_i}\cong T_j\times_{a_j,U_i,t}R_i$, a base change of the etale map $t$; reflexivity makes $t$ surjective. Etaleness descends along the resulting fpqc cover by [lem-galois-fpqc-descend-etale], while surjectivity is checked after the same jointly surjective cover. Therefore $F_i$ is an algebraic space and $U_i\to F_i$ is an etale surjective atlas by [def-trf-algebraic-space].

source.place: Tag 0265 (presentation-quasi-compact), first, second and third proof steps, followed by Tag 02WV.

proof.text: The maps $U_i\to U$ are flat and locally of finite presentation because they are etale; the projections $s,t:R\to U$ are surjective by reflexivity of the equivalence relation and are flat and locally of finite presentation for the same reason. Therefore [lem-trf-etale-relation-finding-opens] applies to each restriction and gives a representable open immersion $F_i\to F$. The images cover $F$: a section of the quotient is fppf-locally represented by a map to $U$, and after refining that cover the inverse image of the affine open covering places the representative in one $U_i$.

The coproduct $\coprod_iF_i$ is an algebraic space by [lem-trf-algebraic-space-coproduct], because the coproduct of the scheme atlases $\coprod_iU_i$ is a scheme. The sheaf $F$ and its open subfunctors $F_i$ satisfy all hypotheses of [lem-trf-algebraic-space-open-gluing]: each $F_i$ is algebraic, each map is representable and open, the family is jointly surjective, and the coproduct is algebraic. Hence $F$ is an algebraic space.

source.place: Tag 02WW, final paragraph, using Tags 02WQ and 02WR.

proof.text:
Because $F$ is now an algebraic space, its diagonal is representable, so for every scheme $T\to F$ the fibre product $T\times_Fh_V$ is a scheme. Choose an fppf cover $T_j\to T$ and representatives $a_j:T_j\to V$ of the given section. The kernel-pair lemma [lem-trf-etale-relation-kernel-pair] gives
$T_j\times_Fh_V\cong T_j\times_{a_j,V,t}R$, a base change of the etale map $t$; reflexivity makes $t$ surjective. Thus the pullback of $q$ to each $T_j$ is etale and surjective, and [lem-galois-fpqc-descend-etale] descends etaleness along the fpqc cover while surjectivity is local on the base. The same kernel-pair isomorphism gives $h_R\cong h_V\times_Fh_V$. Finally, the quotient-sheaf coequalizer definition gives the stated bijection from maps $F\to G$ to maps $h_V\to G$ equalizing $s,t$.

lean.statement: theorem etale_relation_quotient {S : Scheme.{u}} {R V : Over S} (s t : R ⟶ V) [Mono (prod.lift s t)] (hrel : ∀ T : Over S, Equivalence (fun a b : T ⟶ V ↦ ∃ r : T ⟶ R, r ≫ s = a ∧ r ≫ t = b)) [Etale s.left] [Etale t.left] (F : Sheaf (Scheme.fppfTopology.over S) (Type u)) (η : coequalizer (yoneda.map s) (yoneda.map t) ⟶ F.obj) (hη : ∀ G : Sheaf (Scheme.fppfTopology.over S) (Type u), Function.Bijective (fun g : F.obj ⟶ G.obj ↦ η ≫ g)) : IsAlgebraicSpace F ∧ IsEtale (relationQuotientMap s t F η) ∧ IsSurjective (relationQuotientMap s t F η) ∧ IsPullback (yoneda.map s) (yoneda.map t) (relationQuotientMap s t F η) (relationQuotientMap s t F η) ∧ (∀ (T : Over S) (x : F.obj.obj (op T)), ∃ C : Sieve T, C ∈ (Scheme.etaleTopology.over S) T ∧ ∀ (U : Over S) (f : U ⟶ T), C f → ∃ a : U ⟶ V, (relationQuotientMap s t F η).app (op U) a = F.obj.map f.op x) ∧ (∀ (G : Sheaf (Scheme.fppfTopology.over S) (Type u)) (f : yoneda.obj V ⟶ G.obj), yoneda.map s ≫ f = yoneda.map t ≫ f → ∃! g : F.obj ⟶ G.obj, relationQuotientMap s t F η ≫ g = f)
lean.note: The quotient presheaf is the coequalizer of the Yoneda maps. F and its unit η are specified by the sheafification universal property at this presheaf; no global HasWeakSheafify assumption is imposed on the big site. IsPullback expresses that the canonical relation-to-kernel-pair map is an isomorphism. The final unique-factorization clause is the stated bijection on equalizing maps.
